# ax-exit-codes

A tool's exit codes as one table: the overview, every command's footer, `help --json` and the MCP error shape read it, so the numbers never drift. Codes 0, 1 and 2 mean the same thing in every Ouro AX tool.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add ourostack/ouro-ui/ax-exit-codes#v1.3.12
```

It installs `lib/ouro/ax/exit-codes.ts`. Its tests are `ax-exit-codes-tests`. Every item runs on Node 22.18 or later as it is copied: the files import each other as `./<file>.ts`. The [Ouro AX guide](../guides/ax.md) shows how they fit together.

## Exports

### `BASE_EXIT_CODES`

```ts
const BASE_EXIT_CODES: readonly ExitCode[]
```

### `defineExitCodes`

The tool's table: the base codes (their meanings may be reworded, never their names) then its own, numbered from 3 with no gaps.

```ts
function defineExitCodes(codes?: readonly ExitCode[]): ExitTable
```

### `ExitCode`

A tool's exit codes as one table: the overview, every command's footer, `help --json` and the MCP error shape read it, so the numbers never drift. Codes 0, 1 and 2 mean the same thing in every Ouro AX tool.

```ts
interface ExitCode {
  code: number;
  name: string;
  short: string;
  meaning: string;
}
```

### `ExitTable`

```ts
interface ExitTable {
  readonly codes: readonly ExitCode[];
  code(name: string): number;
  has(name: string): boolean;
  line(): string;
}
```

### `FINDINGS_EXIT_CODE`

The code a check or doctor tool declares beside the base codes: its checks ran and found a problem, with a fix beside it. A check that threw before finishing is a crash and exits with the base `error` code instead, so an agent tells "the tool found something" from "the tool broke" by the code alone.

```ts
const FINDINGS_EXIT_CODE: ExitCode
```
